key_insight: Agentic AI populations can partially reproduce real community health behavior patterns, but accuracy is still uneven across places and outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help public health teams simulate screening uptake and test intervention scenarios at the population level, but it is not yet reliable enough to replace observed surveillance data.
method: Built LLMPopSim using U.S. Census and CDC data to create geographically grounded AI agents.
Simulated individual health behaviors and aggregated them to the ZIP Code Tabulation Area level.
Validated on held-out 2022 cohorts from Hawaii and New York State using colorectal cancer screening and mammography.
evidence_signal: Across four state-outcome evaluations, mean absolute error was 3.5 to 15.0 percentage points, with ZCTA-level correlations of 0.26 to 0.69.
watch_item: Performance was worse in lower-prevalence communities, with notable bias and uneven subgroup fidelity, so calibration and fairness checks are essential before use.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
